t: You're looking at the Lyceum Theatre, just off the Strand on Wellington Street. It seats around 2,100 people. The theatre's origins go back to 1765, and over the years the building has hosted a circus, a chapel and London's first waxworks exhibition by Madame Tussauds. After a fire, it was rebuilt to a design by Samuel Beazley and reopened on 14 July 1834. Beazley was the leading theatre architect of his day. The building is unique because it has a balcony overhanging the dress circle. The theatre went on to stage opera and adaptations of Dickens.
